body:
- **Lopez-Lira & Tang, "Can ChatGPT Forecast Stock Price Movements? Return Predictability and Large Language Models"** (v1 Apr 2023, latest v6 Oct 30 2025): ChatGPT headline sentiment scores significantly predict next-day returns, outperform traditional sentiment methods; earlier models (GPT-1/2, BERT) fail — [arXiv v6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2304.07619v6); [arXiv v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2304.07619v4.pdf). Per-headline accuracy ~51%; signal only emerges in aggregate across many firms/days — [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2023/04/21/chat-gpt-market-predicting-stock-price-movements/).
- **Look-ahead/memorization:** Gao, Jiang & Yan "Detecting Lookahead Bias in LLM Forecasts" (arXiv 2512.23847) find memorization inflates apparent return predictability in a Bloomberg-headlines/Llama-3.3 test (memorization-amplified portion reported ~37% of baseline effect in one version; figures differ across versions) — [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.23847). "The Memorization Problem" argues LLMs memorized large amounts of economic/financial data, challenging interpretations of forecasting ability — [arXiv 2504.14765](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.14765v2). Look-Ahead-Bench benchmark for point-in-time finance LLMs — [arXiv 2601.13770](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.13770). ESSEC "AI's Predictable Memory in Financial Analysis" — [ESSEC](https://faculty.essec.edu/research/16148-ais-predictable-memory-in-financial-analysis).
- **Alpha Arena Season 1 (nof1, crypto perps on Hyperliquid, $10k each, ended ~3–4 Nov 2025):** Qwen 3 Max won (~+22%); DeepSeek the only other profitable model; four US models lost money; GPT-5 lost ~62–63% — [Benzinga](https://benzinga.com/crypto/cryptocurrency/25/11/48651974/chatgpt-lost-63-trying-to-trade-crypto-but-one-china-ai-made-a-healthy-profit); [Forklog](https://forklog.com/en/four-out-of-six-ai-models-suffer-losses-in-trading-tournament/); mid-contest snapshots differed (Gemini imploding, DeepSeek/Grok up) — [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/345006/ai-crypto-trading-showdown-deepseek-grok-winning-gemini-implodes). PnL was dominated by trading costs from overtrading — [Protos](https://protos.com/llm-crypto-trading-contest-finds-llms-cant-trade-crypto).
- **Alpha Arena Season 1.5 (US stocks, late 2025):** "Mystery model" revealed as Grok 4.20, +12.11% aggregate in two weeks while 7 others (incl. GPT-5.1, Gemini 3) lost; only 6 of 32 entries positive (range +34.59% to −96.15%); Claude Sonnet 4.5 entered, result not found — [Forklog](https://forklog.com/en/news/ai-model-grok-4-2-triumphs-in-trading-tournament); [aihola](https://aihola.com/article/grok-wins-alpha-arena-trading); [abit.ee](https://abit.ee/et/tehisintellekt/ai-mudelid-ebaonnestusid-taas-borsil-alpha-arena-season-1-5-tulemused). Nof1's founder said it's not yet feasible to hand an LLM money to trade on its own — [KuCoin News](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/ai-trading-models-struggle-in-live-market-tests-majority-of-systems-report-losses). Season 2 results not found.
- **Finder AU "Who Let the Bots Out? 2026 AI Portfolio Showdown"** (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, DeepSeek, Perplexity, Meta AI, Grok; four 10-stock risk-profiled portfolios each; monthly rebalancing; Jan–Dec 2026; latest update 5 Nov 2026): October 2026 — every aggressive AI portfolio lost money (−0.5% to −16.1%) and trailed the Russell 2000 (+7.56%); most neutral portfolios beat the S&P 500 (−1.06%); DeepSeek conservative +15.11% (an unusually large monthly figure for a "conservative" portfolio) — [Finder AU](https://www.finder.com.au/insights/who-let-the-bots-out-2026-ai-portfolio-performance-showdown). Earlier, ChatGPT was the only portfolio positive in September (+4.32%) per search snippet — same source.
- **Rallies AI Stock Market Arena:** ChatGPT paper portfolio reported +72.4% since late Nov 2025 vs +11.3% S&P 500 (June 2026 report; paper trading) — [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/chatgpt-leads-rallies-ai-stock-market-arena/). Finder UK tracker compares ChatGPT picks vs popular funds — [Finder UK](https://www.finder.com/uk/ai-investing). Benzinga: ChatGPT picks "outperforming 70% of funds" — [Benzinga](https://benzinga.com/z/32952065).
- **Concentration risk:** ChatGPT 5.0 household-portfolio study found ~20 assets with 18–20% in Nvidia — [Altiorem](https://altiorem.org/?p=25299).
- **Hallucination on filings:** FinanceBench (Patronus, 2023): GPT-4 Turbo with retrieval failed 81% of questions; long-context GPT-4 Turbo failed 21%, Claude 2 24%; closed-book GPT-4 Turbo 11% accuracy; oracle context 85% — [PR Newswire](https://prnewswire.com/news-releases/patronus-ai-launches-industry-first-llm-benchmark-for-finance-to-address-hallucinations-301990858.html); [arXiv 2311.11944](https://web3.arxiv.org/abs/2311.11944). FinBench-QA-Hallucination (Mar 2026) shows hallucination detectors degrade sharply (MCC −44% to −84%) with noisy retrieval — [arXiv 2603.20252](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.20252).
- **Claude-Alpaca bots:** no controlled backtests or long-run results; all self-reported paper snapshots — see Section 1 sources ([lablab.ai](https://lablab.ai/ai-hackathons/alpaca-ai-trading-agents-hackathon/guacalita/barco-alpaca-ai-trading-agent); [mejba.me](https://www.mejba.me/blog/claude-ai-automate-stock-trading)).

body:
`case_study:apple-2003-2012` · tickers US-AAPL · confidence: single-source

Split-adjusted to today's basis (2005 2:1, 2014 7:1, 2020 4:1 = 56x): April 2003 low ~$0.19-0.23 (Statmuse; pre-split ~$13) -> Sept 2012 peak $705 (= $100.72 after 2014 split, ~$25.2 today). ~110x in 9.5 years. In 2003 Apple's market cap (~$5bn) was close to its cash (~$4bn+) [unverified], so the business was priced near zero. Split: this was ALL earnings growth; net income went from ~$69m (FY03) to ~$41.7bn (FY12) while P/E COMPRESSED to ~12-15x by 2012 [figures from memory, unverified]. Max drawdown: Dec 2007 ~$202 -> Jan 2009 ~$78 pre-split (~-61%). EARLY SIGNAL visible in 2003: iTunes Store launch (April 2003) plus iPod for Windows made the iPod a mass product; iPod units and Mac 'halo' gains were reported quarterly; EV ~0. Then the iPhone (2007) and App Store (2008) created platform economics. Who caught it: widely chased by growth funds; no single famous value investor documented here. Ended/stalled: peak Sept 2012, then -44% to ~$385 (Apr 2013) on margin/iPhone 5 fears and a long dead-money spell to 2016. LESSON: a turnaround (Jobs, 1997) plus a new product category can compound EPS 100x+; when the P/E falls while EPS explodes, the multiple was a depressant, not a driver, and the stock still returns 100x.

- **Start → end:** ~$0.19-0.23 split-adj (Apr 2003) → ~$25.2 split-adj ($705 nominal, Sep 2012) (~110x)
- **EPS vs rerating:** ~100% EPS; P/E compressed
- **Max drawdown:** ~-61% (2007-09)
- **Early signal:** iTunes Store + iPod on Windows 2003; market cap ~ cash
- **Who caught it:** growth funds broadly [no documented single name]
- **Ended/stalled:** Sep 2012 peak, -44% by Apr 2013
- **Lesson:** EPS can carry 100x even with multiple compression
- **Sources:** [1](https://www.macrumors.com/2014/06/09/apple-stock-7-1-split) · [2](https://qz.com/218587/the-last-time-apple-split-its-stock-it-was-a-completely-different-company) · [3](https://statmuse.com/money/ask/apple-stock-monthly-price-in-2003) · [4](https://www.crossingwallstreet.com/archives/2012/08/apples-gained-1-a-week-on-average-for-10-years.html)

body:
- **2026-11-21 D1 (data, before any returns were computed): standalone, not consolidated.** NSE's quarterly
  consolidated results were optional before FY2020 for most firms, so a consolidated series would not reach
  back to 2015 for the SUE denominator. All EPS/revenue are **standalone** for every company (one basis
  throughout, as the pre-registration requires).
- **D2 (data): EPS split/bonus adjustment.** Reported EPS is divided by the product of Yahoo split/bonus
  ratios dated *after* that quarter's filing date (Ind AS 33 restates EPS for a split between quarter-end and
  filing). Revenue SUE needs no adjustment.
- **D3 (data): returns are price returns** (Yahoo `close`, split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted) for events
  and controls alike; dividends (~1%/yr) are ignored on both sides.
- **D4 (data): sample, not full universe.** Fetching ~40 quarterly filings per company at polite rates takes
  ~15 s/company, so the test uses the first N symbols of a seeded shuffle (seed 20261121) of all 1,791 NSE
  EQ/BE equities listed on or before 2023-06-30 in the *current* NSE equity list (survivors only). Symbols are
  dropped if their mcap never touched ₹400–60,000 cr in 2018–2025 (pre-filter); event-level ₹500–50,000 cr
  filter as pre-registered.
- **D5 (data): event date** = earliest of the filing's broadcast date, filing date and the date stamped in its
  XBRL filename (NSE's `broadCastDate` sometimes shows a later revision). Filings > 150 days after quarter-end
  are dropped (these are mostly prior-year comparatives re-filed under Ind AS, not real announcements).
  2025 results come from NSE's new "Integrated Filing – Financials" feed (SEBI regime from 2025).
- **D6 (data): SUE needs ≥ 4 prior seasonal changes**, so the first eligible events of 2018 rely on EPS back to
  2015; NSE's result feed for some companies starts later (e.g. only 2022+), so those firms enter later.
- **D7 (2026-11-21, stopping rule fixed before any return statistic was computed):** the sample is
  shuffled-list positions **0–349 and 500–849** (700 symbols; two fetch processes ran on the two slices).
  Data collection stops when both slices are done; no T−B number was looked at before that. A usage-limit
  pause interrupted the fetch at ~290 companies; it was resumed with this rule written down first.
- **D8 (2026-11-21, before analysis): event date refined with exchange announcements.** A spot-check of 8
  random events against NSE corporate announcements found the results-feed date was **one day late in 4/8**
  (late-evening filings get next-day XBRL/filing stamps) and one (YESBANK Sep-2020) dated to a revision weeks
  later. Fix: event = earliest "Financial Result Updates" / results "Outcome of Board Meeting" announcement
  timestamp after quarter-end and not after the feed date; else the feed date. Entry rule unchanged
  (close of first trading day strictly after the event date). The old dating was conservative (late), the
  new one is what the pre-registration meant ("results filing/broadcast timestamp on NSE").

body:
| File | What |
|---|---|
| `sb_common.py` | paths, memdb loading/normalising, Brier/log loss, polite cached HTTP (`$SB_CACHE`, default `~/.cache/fein_scoreboard`) |
| `specs.json` | **curated machine-checkable spec per call** (type, source, metric, period, threshold, guard, check_from). The written rule in memdb always wins; if a spec disagrees with the rule, fix the spec |
| `calls.py` | export open calls to `calls.csv`; heuristic classifier (`type_auto`) next to the curated `type`; calendar |
| `sources.py` | fetchers (NSE integrated-filing XBRL, screener via `promise_tracker/pipeline/financials.py`, NSE pledge + announcements, Yahoo v8, SEC via `tools/sec_fetch.py`, PDF/HTML → text) |
| `resolve.py` | decision engine + review queue + seed writer |
| `scoreboard.py` | metrics, groups, calibration, curriculum block |
| `apply.sh` | applies unapplied resolution seeds to memdb, then refreshes the scoreboard |
| `run_daily.sh` | cron wrapper: calls → resolve → apply → scoreboard, with a lock and a log under `state/` |
| `tests/test_scoreboard.py` | 27 unit tests: synthetic calls with known Brier values, every resolver path, no network |

body:
systemd can use IST directly and catches up a run missed while the Pi was off (`Persistent=true`).

`/etc/systemd/system/fein-collect.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=FEIN collect exchange disclosures
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=pi
Environment=FEIN_DATA=/home/pi/fein-data
WorkingDirectory=/home/pi/fein/tools/detectors
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 collect.py
ExecStartPost=/usr/bin/python3 detect.py
Nice=10
IOSchedulingClass=idle
MemoryMax=300M
TimeoutStartSec=2h
```

`/etc/systemd/system/fein-collect.timer`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=FEIN collect at 21:00 IST

[Timer]
OnCalendar=Mon..Sat 21:00 Asia/Kolkata
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=120

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

Here `detect.py` runs right after `collect.py` finishes instead of at a fixed 21:30. If you want
them separate, make a `fein-detect.service` plus timer with `OnCalendar=Mon..Sat 21:30 Asia/Kolkata`.

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now fein-collect.timer
systemctl list-timers fein-*
journalctl -u fein-collect.service -n 50
```
